about.heroSubtext: I'm a design leader directing complex products, building the teams that ship them, and turning AI from a tool into how teams work.
about.bio: Howdy! I'm a design leader based in Richmond, VA, focused on building user-centered products and the teams that ship them. I've spent my career moving from craft to strategy, and now I'm directing design across complex, multi-stakeholder engagements while building the skills that take leaders from execution to creative vision. I'm not interested in maintaining the status quo; I'm here to raise the bar.

humanStuff.body: When I'm not in meetings or mentoring designers, you'll find me diving into video games, debating sneaker drops, or breaking down zone defenses. I'm a new dad and have fully embraced this chapter, tucked-in t-shirts and all. I'm also a pet parent to two huskies and a cat; they keep me grounded and occasionally interrupt video calls.
humanStuff.pullQuote: Once upon a time, I dreamt of becoming a professional bowler like Norm Duke. That didn't pan out, but the focus, precision, and competitive drive stuck with me.
humanStuff.pullQuoteAttr: I still bowl today, just not professionally. Ask if you're curious!

setsApart.heading:
Economics, sales,
and then design.
paragraphs: What sets me apart is a diversified background in economics and sales. I don't just understand how to build great experiences; I understand how to articulate their business value. I'm as comfortable in a boardroom discussing ROI as I am in a design review discussing hierarchy and interaction patterns. That fluency makes me effective at aligning stakeholders, securing buy-in, and ensuring design decisions are made with business context... not just defended from outside it.

My foundation is classic double-diamond thinking, but my application has evolved. I focus less on personal craft and more on building systems, processes, and teams that consistently deliver user-centered outcomes. Before design, I was in sales advocating for technology adoption. My job wasn't pushing products, it was making them indispensable. That mindset still drives me.

howIWork.heading:
AI as a strategic multiplier,
not a shortcut.
paragraphs: I've led design in both Waterfall and Agile environments and know how to partner with engineering and product to find the right process for the problem, not force a methodology where it doesn't fit.

AI is now central to how I work. And the real opportunity isn't individual efficiency, it's reshaping how teams operate. If you're thinking about how AI changes the design practice at an organizational level, that's a conversation I'm ready to have.

columns.heading: Discovery & Research
items: Stakeholder interviews to understand business goals and constraints
User research to uncover real needs and pain points
Competitive analysis to identify opportunities and patterns

columns.heading: AI-Powered Content Analysis
items: Analyze existing content for patterns and gaps
Extract key themes from user feedback at scale
Generate initial content inventories and audit reports
columns.note: In practice: On a recent e-commerce redesign, I fed an entire website into ChatGPT to identify the top 10 friction points in the primary user flow — work that would've taken weeks happened in an afternoon.

columns.heading: Heuristic Evaluation
items: Nielsen's 10 usability heuristics
Accessibility standards (WCAG 2.2)
Industry-specific best practices

columns.heading: Information Architecture
items: Content buckets that group related information logically
User flow diagrams showing key pathways
Sitemaps that visualize the entire information ecosystem
columns.note: A core belief: Good IA is invisible — users should find what they need without thinking about how it's organized. When navigation becomes the subject, something has already gone wrong.

columns.heading: Wireframing & Prototyping
items: Lo-fi wireframes to test information hierarchy
High-fidelity wireframes for design system work
Interactive prototypes for usability testing

columns.heading: Design System Thinking
items: Creating reusable component libraries
Documenting interaction patterns
Establishing design tokens for consistency
columns.note: The reason this matters: It's not just about efficiency. It's about creating experiences that feel cohesive across every touchpoint — whether someone is on the homepage or a deeply nested product page.

columns.heading: Developer Partnership
items: Co-creating during the design phase to ensure feasibility
Providing detailed specs with interaction states and edge cases
Participating in sprint planning to prioritize features
Conducting design QA during implementation

columns.heading: Iterative Improvement
items: Monitor analytics and user feedback post-launch
Conduct usability testing on live products
Create optimization roadmaps based on data
columns.note: The work doesn't end at launch. The best products I've shipped have been improved meaningfully in the 90 days after go-live — because that's when real usage data starts telling the truth.
columns.noteBold: The work doesn't end at launch.

principles.title:
AI-Augmented,
Human-Centered
principles.body: AI accelerates the work — synthesis, content analysis, logic mapping. But it doesn't replace the judgment calls. Every AI output runs through a human lens before it informs a decision.

principles.title:
Systems Over
Screens
principles.body: I design patterns and components, not just individual interfaces. A screen is a snapshot. A system is a strategy — and it's what makes design scale without falling apart.

principles.title:
Collaborative
by Design
principles.body: Stakeholders, developers, and users aren't interruptions to the process — they're inputs to it. The best design decisions I've made came from conversations I didn't expect to matter.

principles.title:
Data-Informed,
Not Data-Driven
principles.body: Numbers tell you what happened. Research tells you why. I balance quantitative signals with qualitative understanding — because optimizing for metrics alone often produces products that test well and feel wrong.
